label: late original-phase input of d (or b/e/w/k/m/v after a digit/j/g/i/n/c-heavy prefix)
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, never on <DEL> or copy steps, and never at t=0-1; rate rises with position, peaking at orig_idx 5-6 (near the end of the input). It is input-token selective: 'd' carries 47% of activation mass (12x lift) and all top activations are on 'd'; b, e, w, k, m, v (and weakly 3, s) make up most of the rest; nearly silent on other tokens. Whether it fires on a given 'd' depends on the prefix: it is more likely when earlier inputs include digits 0/1/2 or j, g, i, n, c (first token 0 gives 4.7x lift), and less likely when they include k, l, r, s, w, x, 3, b, m. First occurrences of a token fire much more than repeats (in_first lift 1.7x vs 0.2x). The predicate (late original-phase d, or one of the secondary tokens after an enhancer-dominated prefix) gets about 86% of activation mass but only ~29% precision on dev: the prefix dependence looks graded and spread across many tokens, and a simple count does not capture it, so most predicted 'd' steps stay below threshold.
